----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- COMPLETIONIST - IN-GAME TEXT
-- File: Completionist_Translations_M.txt   (shout hints, Stones of Barenziah, log text, window text)
--
-- Each line is:   KEY <TAB> | text
--
-- HOW TO TRANSLATE
--   * Change only the text AFTER the '|'. Never change the KEY in front of it.
--   * Keep the TAB between the KEY and the '|': a key ends at its first TAB.
--   * '\n' is a line break. Keep each one where it is.
--   * Keep '~~~ Name ~~~' headings and placeholders such as {} exactly as they are.
--   * Some texts end in a space on purpose (for example Completed: ). Keep that space,
--     because Completionist puts a name straight after it.
--   * Lines starting with '-' are comments and are ignored.
--   * The order of the lines does not matter: lines are matched by KEY.
--   * Set your editor's tab width to 4 and the columns line up.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Stones of Barenziah: where to find them
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Barenziah_Text00	|~~~ Ansilvund ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located on the table at the end of the Ansilvund Burial Chambers.
Barenziah_Text01	|~~~ Black-Briar Lodge ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the top floor bedroom, next to the bed.
Barenziah_Text02	|~~~ College of Winterhold ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the Arch-Mage Quarters.
Barenziah_Text03	|~~~ Dainty Sload ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the last room on the table.
Barenziah_Text04	|~~~ Dark Brotherhood Sanctuary ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located on the dresser in Astrid's room.
Barenziah_Text05	|~~~ Dead Crone Rock ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located on the stone altar opposite the Word Wall.
Barenziah_Text06	|~~~ Fellglow Keep ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located straight up the stairs on the right-hand side.
Barenziah_Text07	|~~~ Hob's Fall Cave ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located near the alchemy set under the bridge in the northwestern part of the cave system.
Barenziah_Text08	|~~~ Treasury House ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the Treasury House on a bedside table in Thonar's bedroom.
Barenziah_Text09	|~~~ Dwemer Museum ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in Understone Keep's Dwemer Museum, on a table in the first room to the left.
Barenziah_Text10	|~~~ Pinewatch ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the basement. Press the hidden button to the right of the bookcase, which provides access to the bandits' hideout. The stone is found in a locked room in the Bandit's Sanctuary.
Barenziah_Text11	|~~~ Rannveig's Fast ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located next to the alchemy lab and chest on the right after falling down the trapdoor in front of the chest and the Word Wall.
Barenziah_Text12	|~~~ Mistveil Keep ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in Mistveil Keep in the Jarl's bedroom. Go up the stairs and through the locked centre door. It will be on the end table left of the bed.
Barenziah_Text13	|~~~ Blue Palace ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the Blue Palace in the Jarl's bedroom, on top of the wardrobe to the right of the bed.
Barenziah_Text14	|~~~ Proudspire Manor ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in Proudspire Manor. You must first purchase the house. The stone can be found on the top floor in the master bedroom, on top of the wardrobe behind the door.
Barenziah_Text15	|~~~ Stony Creek Cave ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located on the table next to the alchemy lab in the room off to the side.
Barenziah_Text16	|~~~ Sunderstone Gorge ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located on the table with two bodies in front of the Word Wall.
Barenziah_Text17	|~~~ Thalmor Embassy / Reeking Cave ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the Thalmor Embassy in Elenwen's Solar on the second floor, or inside Reeking Cave next to a corpse in the back, depending on your Skyrim version.
Barenziah_Text18	|~~~ Whiterun Hall of the Dead ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located inside the Hall of the Dead Catacombs. Go down the left stairs and it will be to your left, next to a skeleton.
Barenziah_Text19	|~~~ Dragonsreach ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in Dragonsreach in the Jarl's bedroom, on the right-hand end table.
Barenziah_Text20	|~~~ Jorrvaskr ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in Jorrvaskr's living quarters, on the bookshelf in Kodlak's room.
Barenziah_Text21	|~~~ House of Clan Shatter-Shield ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the House of Clan Shatter-Shield, on a bookshelf in the room to the left of the top of the stairs.
Barenziah_Text22	|~~~ Palace of the Kings ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the Palace of the Kings Upstairs. Take the first door to the left upon entering the main palace area, then find Wuunferth's room with an Alchemy Lab & Arcane Enchanter at the end of the hall. The stone is on a table on the right side of the room.
Barenziah_Text23	|~~~ Yngvild ~~~\nThis Stone of Barenziah can be located in the bedroom behind the throne in the Yngvild throne room.

UI_Setting_Reset				|Reset to defaults
UI_Setting_ResetRow				|Window settings
UI_SettingHint_Reset			|Puts the window's settings back to how they started, including where the notifications sit. Your keyboard keys are kept.

-- In-game window: text and settings (part 3)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
UI_Setting_CellKey					|Cell Scanner key
UI_SettingHint_CellKey				|Opens the Cell Scanner: what's still to collect in the cell you're in. Press Delete while it waits to leave it unbound.
UI_Setting_CellPad					|Cell Scanner (controller)
UI_SettingHint_CellPad				|Button combo that opens the Cell Scanner. Press Delete while it waits to leave it unbound.
UI_Cell_NearestHeader				|Mark Nearest
UI_Setting_NearestKey				|Mark nearest find key
UI_SettingHint_NearestKey			|While you play, marks the nearest thing still to collect and puts an objective on it. Press it again to cancel that marker, then again for the next nearest. Press Delete while it waits to leave it unbound.
UI_Setting_NearestPad				|Mark nearest find (controller)
UI_SettingHint_NearestPad			|Button combo that marks the nearest thing still to collect while you play. Press it again to cancel that marker, then again for the next nearest. Press Delete while it waits to leave it unbound.
UI_Setting_SweepEffect				|Scan sweep effect
UI_SettingHint_SweepEffect			|When you mark the nearest find, a wave runs out from you over the world and things still to collect catch the light as it reaches them. Off still marks it, with no effect.
UI_Cell_AllMarked					|Everything left to find here is already marked.
UI_Setting_SeekersWhisper			|Learn the Seeker's Whisper shout
UI_SettingHint_SeekersWhisper		|Gives you a quiet shout with all three words, no dragon souls needed: equip it in the Magic menu and use it like any other. Each shout moves your marker straight to the next nearest find and sends out the wave, even with Scan sweep effect off. Hold it longer for more words: about 115 m, 230 m or 570 m, with a longer cooldown each time. Off takes the shout away again.
UI_Shout_Name						|Seeker's Whisper
UI_Shout_Description				|Sends a wave out from you that lights up what's still to collect and marks the nearest. More words reach further.

UI_Dragons_Lore_Alduin				|The first-born of Akatosh, the World-Eater of Nord legend. Long ago he ruled Skyrim through his dragon priests, until the ancient Tongues used an Elder Scroll to cast him out of time. He returns at Helgen as the game begins, raises the dead dragons from their burial mounds, and hides in Sovngarde to feed on the souls of the dead. With the heroes Gormlaith, Hakon and Felldir you defeat him there in Dragonslayer.
UI_Dragons_Meaning_Paarthurnax		|Ambition Overlord Cruelty

For thousands of years since, he has lived on the mountain as master of the Greybeards, following the Way of the Voice to keep his cruel nature in check. He teaches you Fire Breath and how Alduin was beaten before. The Blades want him dead for his old crimes: you can kill him for them, or spare him and he stays on his mountain.

Seeing that Alduin is losing, he tells you Alduin has gone to Skuldafn and agrees to fly you there in return for his freedom. Once free he answers your Call Dragon shout and fights at your side.

It has no name of its own, but it is the only one of its kind in the game, and it is too big to follow you back through the gate.

UI_Achievements_Goal_2								|Complete "Bleak Falls Barrow"
UI_Achievements_Tip_2								|Farengar in Dragonsreach sends you for the Dragonstone. The door at the end of the barrow opens with the Golden Claw: the right order of animals is drawn on the claw's palm.
UI_Achievements_Name_3								|The Way of the Voice
UI_Achievements_Goal_3								|Complete "The Way of the Voice"
UI_Achievements_Tip_3								|After Dragon Rising, climb the 7,000 steps from Ivarstead to High Hrothgar and do the Greybeards' trials. They also teach you the rest of Unrelenting Force on the way.
UI_Achievements_Name_4								|Diplomatic Immunity
UI_Achievements_Goal_4								|Complete "Diplomatic Immunity"
UI_Achievements_Tip_4								|Delphine sends you into the Thalmor Embassy's party. You go in without your gear, so choose well what Malborn smuggles in for you: a weapon, armour and a few potions.
UI_Achievements_Name_5								|Alduin's Wall
UI_Achievements_Goal_5								|Complete "Alduin's Wall"
UI_Achievements_Tip_5								|Find Esbern in the Ratway Warrens under Riften, then go with him and Delphine to Sky Haven Temple in Karthspire. The temple door opens to the Dragonborn's blood.
UI_Achievements_Name_6								|Elder Knowledge
UI_Achievements_Goal_6								|Complete "Elder Knowledge"
UI_Achievements_Tip_6								|Septimus Signus, on the ice north of Winterhold, sends you through Alftand to Blackreach. Look around while you're down there: Blackreach has the Crimson Nirnroot that Sinderion wants.
UI_Achievements_Name_7								|The Fallen
UI_Achievements_Goal_7								|Complete "The Fallen"
UI_Achievements_Tip_7								|If the civil war has started, the Jarl of Whiterun won't let you trap a dragon in Dragonsreach until the peace council in Season Unending has met. Finish the civil war first or go to the council.
UI_Achievements_Name_8								|Dragonslayer
UI_Achievements_Goal_8								|Complete "Dragonslayer"
UI_Achievements_Tip_8								|Odahviing flies you to Skuldafn and you go on to Sovngarde. You come back to Skyrim afterwards, so nothing is lost by going.
UI_Achievements_Name_9								|Take Up Arms
UI_Achievements_Goal_9								|Join the Companions
UI_Achievements_Tip_9								|Go to Jorrvaskr in Whiterun, speak to Kodlak, then spar with Vilkas in the yard.
UI_Achievements_Name_10								|Blood Oath
UI_Achievements_Goal_10								|Become a member of the Circle
UI_Achievements_Tip_10								|Comes early in the Companions' story, when Skjor offers you the beast blood in the Underforge. You become a werewolf, which also starts you towards Werewolf Mastered.
UI_Achievements_Name_11								|Glory of the Dead
UI_Achievements_Goal_11								|Complete "Glory of the Dead"
UI_Achievements_Tip_11								|The end of the Companions' story, at Ysgramor's Tomb.
UI_Achievements_Name_12								|Gatekeeper
UI_Achievements_Goal_12								|Join the College of Winterhold
UI_Achievements_Tip_12								|Ride or walk to Winterhold and speak to Faralda at the bridge. She asks you to cast a spell (she'll sell you one if you have none), or you can talk your way in.
UI_Achievements_Name_13								|Revealing the Unseen
UI_Achievements_Goal_13								|Complete "Revealing the Unseen"
UI_Achievements_Tip_13								|Part of the College's story: after Saarthal, it takes you to Mzulft with the Synod.
UI_Achievements_Name_14								|The Eye of Magnus
UI_Achievements_Goal_14								|Complete "The Eye of Magnus"
UI_Achievements_Tip_14								|The end of the College of Winterhold's story.
UI_Achievements_Name_15								|Taking Care of Business
UI_Achievements_Goal_15								|Join the Thieves Guild
UI_Achievements_Tip_15								|Brynjolf in Riften's marketplace gives you the job with Madesi's ring, then sends you to collect three debts for the guild.
UI_Achievements_Name_16								|Darkness Returns
UI_Achievements_Goal_16								|Complete "Darkness Returns"
UI_Achievements_Tip_16								|Part of the Thieves Guild's story, near the end: the Skeleton Key goes back to the Twilight Sepulcher.
UI_Achievements_Name_17								|One with the Shadows
UI_Achievements_Goal_17								|Returned the Thieves Guild to its former glory
UI_Achievements_Tip_17								|Do Delvin's and Vex's small jobs in Whiterun, Windhelm, Markarth and Solitude. Five in one city opens that city's big job; do all four. Keep Erikur in Solitude alive until The Dainty Sload is done.
UI_Achievements_Name_18								|With Friends Like These...
UI_Achievements_Goal_18								|Join the Dark Brotherhood
UI_Achievements_Tip_18								|Speak to Aventus Aretino in Windhelm about the Black Sacrament, or wait for the Dark Brotherhood to find you after a murder. Destroying the Brotherhood locks this one out, so don't kill Astrid at the shack.
UI_Achievements_Name_19								|Bound Until Death
UI_Achievements_Goal_19								|Complete "Bound Until Death"
UI_Achievements_Tip_19								|A Dark Brotherhood contract: Vittoria Vici, killed at her own wedding in Solitude. Gone if you destroy the Brotherhood.
UI_Achievements_Name_20								|Hail Sithis!
UI_Achievements_Goal_20								|Complete "Hail Sithis!"
UI_Achievements_Tip_20								|The end of the Dark Brotherhood's story. Gone if you destroy the Brotherhood.
UI_Achievements_Name_21								|Taking Sides
UI_Achievements_Goal_21								|Join the Stormcloaks or the Imperial Army
UI_Achievements_Tip_21								|Join Ulfric's Stormcloaks in Windhelm or General Tullius's Legion in Solitude. Either side counts.
UI_Achievements_Name_22								|War Hero
UI_Achievements_Goal_22								|Capture Fort Sungard or Fort Greenwall
UI_Achievements_Tip_22								|Comes with taking Fort Sungard in the Reach as a Stormcloak, or Fort Greenwall in the Rift for the Legion. Giving that hold away at the peace council in Season Unending can take the battle away.
UI_Achievements_Name_23								|Hero of Skyrim
UI_Achievements_Goal_23								|Capture Solitude or Windhelm
UI_Achievements_Tip_23								|The end of the civil war, at Solitude or Windhelm.
UI_Achievements_Name_24								|Sideways
UI_Achievements_Goal_24								|Complete 10 side quests
UI_Achievements_Tip_24								|Side quests are the ones on their own in the journal, not part of a story. Town quests from innkeepers and Jarls are the quickest.
UI_Achievements_Name_25								|Hero of the People
UI_Achievements_Goal_25								|Complete 50 Misc Objectives
UI_Achievements_Tip_25								|Miscellaneous objectives are the small tasks in the journal: favours, deliveries and fetching things. Every innkeeper and steward has a few.
UI_Achievements_Name_26								|Hard Worker
UI_Achievements_Goal_26								|Chop wood, mine ore, and cook food
UI_Achievements_Tip_26								|All three can be done in Riverwood: chop wood at the block by the mill, mine the ore vein near the smithy with a pickaxe, and cook at any cooking pot.
UI_Achievements_Name_27								|Thief
UI_Achievements_Goal_27								|Pick 50 locks and 50 pockets
UI_Achievements_Tip_27								|Any lock and any successful pickpocket counts. Novice locks and lifting a coin purse are quick; save before the pockets.
UI_Achievements_Name_28								|Snake Tongue
UI_Achievements_Goal_28								|Successfully persuade, bribe, and intimidate
UI_Achievements_Tip_28								|Look for (Persuade), (Bribe) and (Intimidate) in dialogue; one success of each. A higher Speech skill and a few Speech perks make them easier.
UI_Achievements_Name_29								|Blessed
UI_Achievements_Goal_29								|Select a Standing Stone blessing
UI_Achievements_Tip_29								|Use any standing stone. The Guardian Stones on the road from Helgen to Riverwood are the first you come to.
UI_Achievements_Name_30								|Standing Stones
UI_Achievements_Goal_30								|Find 13 Standing Stones
UI_Achievements_Tip_30								|Each stone counts once, and the three Guardian Stones by Riverwood count as three on their own. The game adds them up as you find them; the Standing Stones page shows which you've been to.
UI_Achievements_Name_31								|Citizen
UI_Achievements_Goal_31								|Buy a house
UI_Achievements_Tip_31								|Breezehome in Whiterun costs 5,000 gold once you've done Dragon Rising: buy it from Proventus Avenicci in Dragonsreach. Hearthfire land counts too.
UI_Achievements_Name_32								|Wanted
UI_Achievements_Goal_32								|Escape from jail
UI_Achievements_Tip_32								|Keep a lockpick on you: the guards leave you one. Get arrested, choose jail, pick the cell door and get out. Markarth's Cidhna Mine has its own escape quest.
UI_Achievements_Name_33								|Married
UI_Achievements_Goal_33								|Get married
UI_Achievements_Tip_33								|Buy an Amulet of Mara from Maramal at the Temple of Mara in Riften, wear it, and talk to someone who can marry you. The wedding is at the temple.
UI_Achievements_Name_34								|Artificer
UI_Achievements_Goal_34								|Make a smithed item, an enchanted item, and a potion
UI_Achievements_Tip_34								|Make anything at a forge, enchant anything at an arcane enchanter (disenchant something first to learn an enchantment), and mix any potion or poison at an alchemy lab. Whiterun has all three.
UI_Achievements_Name_35								|Master Criminal
UI_Achievements_Goal_35								|Bounty of 1000 gold in all nine holds
UI_Achievements_Tip_35								|A bounty of 1,000 gold in each of the nine holds at some point. You can pay it off afterwards: it only has to reach 1,000 once.
UI_Achievements_Name_36								|Golden Touch
UI_Achievements_Goal_36								|Have 100,000 gold
UI_Achievements_Tip_36								|Only gold you carry counts, not gold in a chest. Selling what you smith or enchant, and the Speech perk that lets you invest in shops, get you there fastest.
UI_Achievements_Name_37								|Delver
UI_Achievements_Goal_37								|Clear 50 dungeons
UI_Achievements_Tip_37								|A dungeon is cleared when its boss is dead. Bounty and radiant quests send you to ones you haven't done.
UI_Achievements_Name_38								|Skill Master
UI_Achievements_Goal_38								|Get a skill to 100
UI_Achievements_Tip_38								|Despite its description, the game gives this one after 100 skill increases in total, across all your skills, not for one skill at 100. Trainers' lessons count too; the Trainers page shows who teaches what.
UI_Achievements_Name_39								|Explorer
UI_Achievements_Goal_39								|Discover 100 Locations
UI_Achievements_Tip_39								|Every map marker you find counts. The Locations pages show what's left.
UI_Achievements_Name_40								|Reader
UI_Achievements_Goal_40								|Read 50 Skill Books
UI_Achievements_Tip_40								|Each skill book counts once, the first time you read it. Many are on shop shelves: buying and reading them counts.
UI_Achievements_Name_41								|Daedric Influence
UI_Achievements_Goal_41								|Acquire a Daedric Artifact
UI_Achievements_Tip_41								|Comes with the first Daedric artefact, from a Daedric quest or found in the world, such as Meridia's Beacon.
UI_Achievements_Name_42								|Oblivion Walker
UI_Achievements_Goal_42								|Collect 15 Daedric Artifacts
UI_Achievements_Tip_42								|An artefact counts when you get it, so you can store or sell it after. Where a Daedric quest ends with a choice, take the side that gives the artefact.
UI_Achievements_Name_43								|Dragon Soul
UI_Achievements_Goal_43								|Absorb a dragon soul
UI_Achievements_Tip_43								|The first dragon, at the Western Watchtower during Dragon Rising.
UI_Achievements_Name_44								|Dragon Hunter
UI_Achievements_Goal_44								|Absorb 20 dragon souls
UI_Achievements_Tip_44								|Dragons come more often once the main story has reached Alduin's Wall. The Dragons page keeps count of the dragons you've killed.
UI_Achievements_Name_45								|Words of Power
UI_Achievements_Goal_45								|Learn all three words of a shout
UI_Achievements_Tip_45								|You learn all three words of Unrelenting Force during The Way of the Voice, so this usually comes on its own.
UI_Achievements_Name_46								|Thu'um Master
UI_Achievements_Goal_46								|Learn 20 shouts
UI_Achievements_Tip_46								|Twenty different shouts. The Shouts page shows every word wall, and which words you still need.
UI_Achievements_Name_47								|Apprentice
UI_Achievements_Goal_47								|Reach Level 5
UI_Achievements_Tip_47								|Level 5.
UI_Achievements_Name_48								|Adept
UI_Achievements_Goal_48								|Reach Level 10
UI_Achievements_Tip_48								|Level 10.
UI_Achievements_Name_49								|Expert
UI_Achievements_Goal_49								|Reach Level 25
UI_Achievements_Tip_49								|Level 25.
UI_Achievements_Name_50								|Master
UI_Achievements_Goal_50								|Reach Level 50
UI_Achievements_Tip_50								|Level 50. Skills made legendary still raise your level, so you can keep going.
UI_Achievements_Name_51								|Awakening
UI_Achievements_Goal_51								|Complete "Awakening"
UI_Achievements_Tip_51								|The start of Dawnguard: join the Dawnguard at Fort Dawnguard, then wake Serana in Dimhollow Crypt.
UI_Achievements_Name_52								|Beyond Death
UI_Achievements_Goal_52								|Complete "Beyond Death"
UI_Achievements_Tip_52								|Serana's mother is in the Soul Cairn. Going in costs part of your soul, unless you're a vampire.
UI_Achievements_Name_53								|Kindred Judgment
UI_Achievements_Goal_53								|Complete "Kindred Judgment"
UI_Achievements_Tip_53								|The end of Dawnguard, on either side.
UI_Achievements_Name_54								|Lost to the Ages
UI_Achievements_Goal_54								|Complete "Lost to the Ages"
UI_Achievements_Tip_54								|Comes with the Aetherium Forge. Lost to the Ages takes you to Arkngthamz in the Reach, where Katria helps you find the shards.
UI_Achievements_Name_55								|Soul Tear
UI_Achievements_Goal_55								|Learn all three words of Soul Tear
UI_Achievements_Tip_55								|Summon Durnehviir in Skyrim three times: he teaches you one word of Soul Tear each time. You learn to summon him in the Soul Cairn.
UI_Achievements_Name_56								|Auriel's Bow
UI_Achievements_Goal_56								|Use the special power of Auriel's Bow
UI_Achievements_Tip_56								|Fire a Sunhallowed or Bloodcursed elven arrow at the sun with Auriel's Bow. The bow isn't a quest item once Dawnguard is done, so don't sell it or leave it lying around.
UI_Achievements_Name_57								|Werewolf Mastered
UI_Achievements_Goal_57								|Acquire 11 werewolf perks
UI_Achievements_Tip_57								|Werewolf perks come from feeding on corpses in beast form. Curing lycanthropy twice locks you out of this, and becoming a Vampire Lord counts as a cure.
UI_Achievements_Name_58								|Vampire Mastered
UI_Achievements_Goal_58								|Acquire 11 vampire perks
UI_Achievements_Tip_58								|Vampire Lord perks come from draining and biting in Vampire Lord form.
UI_Achievements_Name_59								|A New You
UI_Achievements_Goal_59								|Change your face
UI_Achievements_Tip_59								|Galathil, the face sculptor, sits in the Ragged Flagon under Riften. Innkeepers and guards mention her once Dawnguard is installed.
UI_Achievements_Name_60								|Legend
UI_Achievements_Goal_60								|Defeat a Legendary Dragon
UI_Achievements_Tip_60								|Legendary dragons only appear once you reach level 78. Kills count here from when Completionist started counting dragon kills.
UI_Achievements_Name_61								|Proud Parent
UI_Achievements_Goal_61								|Adopt a child
UI_Achievements_Tip_61								|Adopt a child from Honorhall Orphanage in Riften or from Whiterun's streets. Your home needs a child's bedroom first.
UI_Achievements_Name_62								|Landowner
UI_Achievements_Goal_62								|Buy a plot of land
UI_Achievements_Tip_62								|Buy land from the steward in Falkreath, Morthal or Dawnstar. The Jarl has to like you first, usually after a task for them.
UI_Achievements_Name_63								|Architect
UI_Achievements_Goal_63								|Build three wings on a house
UI_Achievements_Tip_63								|Build any three wings on one Hearthfire house.
UI_Achievements_Name_64								|Land Baron
UI_Achievements_Goal_64								|Buy three plots of land
UI_Achievements_Tip_64								|Buy all three plots: Lakeview Manor, Windstad Manor and Heljarchen Hall.
UI_Achievements_Name_65								|Master Architect
UI_Achievements_Goal_65								|Build three houses
UI_Achievements_Tip_65								|Build a house on all three Hearthfire plots.
UI_Achievements_Name_66								|Outlander
UI_Achievements_Goal_66								|Arrive on Solstheim
UI_Achievements_Tip_66								|Take the Northern Maiden from Windhelm's docks to Raven Rock.
UI_Achievements_Name_67								|The Temple of Miraak
UI_Achievements_Goal_67								|Complete "The Temple of Miraak"
UI_Achievements_Tip_67								|The first part of the Dragonborn story, after the cultists in Raven Rock.
UI_Achievements_Name_68								|The Path of Knowledge
UI_Achievements_Goal_68								|Complete "The Path of Knowledge"
UI_Achievements_Tip_68								|The second part of the Dragonborn story, ending in Apocrypha.
UI_Achievements_Name_69								|At the Summit of Apocrypha
UI_Achievements_Goal_69								|Complete "At the Summit of Apocrypha"
UI_Achievements_Tip_69								|The end of the Dragonborn story.
UI_Achievements_Name_70								|Dragon Aspect
UI_Achievements_Goal_70								|Learn all 3 words of Dragon Aspect
UI_Achievements_Tip_70								|Its words are found during the Dragonborn story and on Solstheim. The Shouts page shows where.
UI_Achievements_Name_71								|Hidden Knowledge
UI_Achievements_Goal_71								|Learn the secrets of 5 Black Books
UI_Achievements_Tip_71								|Read Black Books on Solstheim to the end of each and pick a reward. Five of the seven are enough.
UI_Achievements_Name_72								|Stalhrim Crafter
UI_Achievements_Goal_72								|Craft an item out of Stalhrim
UI_Achievements_Tip_72								|Ask Deor Woodcutter or Fanari Strong-Voice in Raven Rock about stalhrim; A New Source of Stalhrim ends with Baldor Iron-Shaper teaching you. Smithing stalhrim needs the Ebony Smithing perk. The quest is lost if both of them die.
UI_Achievements_Name_73								|Dragonrider
UI_Achievements_Goal_73								|Tame and ride 5 dragons
UI_Achievements_Tip_73								|Use Bend Will on a dragon and ride it, with five dragons. Bend Will is learnt during the Dragonborn story.
UI_Achievements_Name_74								|Raven Rock Owner
UI_Achievements_Goal_74								|Own a house in Raven Rock
UI_Achievements_Tip_74								|Help Adril Arano in Served Cold and Severin Manor is yours, free.
UI_Achievements_Name_75								|Solstheim Explorer
UI_Achievements_Goal_75								|Discover 30 locations on the island of Solstheim
UI_Achievements_Tip_75								|Any 30 map markers on Solstheim.
UI_Achievements_Stat_Holds							|Holds at 1,000 bounty now

-- UI: Achievements (UI_Achievements_*)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
UI_Achievements_SettingsTracking	|Achievements
UI_Achievements_SettingsDetails		|Achievement Details
UI_Achievements_SettingShow			|Show the Achievements page
UI_Achievements_SettingShowInfo		|Shows your achievements in the sidebar. Off hides the page.
UI_Achievements_SettingProgress		|This save's progress
UI_Achievements_SettingProgressInfo	|Shows how far this save is towards each one, from the counts the game keeps.
UI_Achievements_SettingTips			|How to get it
UI_Achievements_SettingTipsInfo		|Shows a tip for each one. Some name places and people from the quests.
UI_Achievements_SettingRarity		|How rare it is
UI_Achievements_SettingRarityInfo	|Shows how many players have each one, from Steam.

UI_Ingredients_Poison					|Poison
UI_Ingredients_HintEat					|Eat one to learn it

UI_Ingredients_HintShared{}				|Shared with {}
UI_Ingredients_HintNone					|Nothing you carry shares it
UI_Ingredients_HintOnly					|No other ingredient has it

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- UI: Ingredient lore (UI_Ingredients_Lore_*)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
UI_Ingredients_Lore_AbeceanLongfin			|A slim, silvery fish named after the Abecean Sea off Cyrodiil's western coast. In Skyrim it swims the rivers and lakes, and a quick hand can catch one straight out of the water.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BearClaws				|Taken from the bears that roam Skyrim's forests and caves. Hunters keep them as trophies, and alchemists grind them into draughts said to lend the drinker a little of a bear's strength.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Bee						|A honeybee, caught as it drifts between the flowers or taken from a hive. Its sting is small, but an alchemist can make a good deal more of it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BeehiveHusk				|The papery shell of a beehive. Skyrim has few apiaries, and the biggest hives in the land are kept at Goldenglow Estate, on its island near Riften.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BeritsAshes				|The ashes of Berit, a Falkreath man and an old friend of Thadgeir's, kept in Dengeir's House in Falkreath. To an alchemist they're no different from bone meal, which is perhaps not how Berit hoped to be remembered.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BleedingCrown			|A cave fungus that grows in clusters in damp caves and old ruins, its broad caps easy to spot by torchlight. It leaves a target weaker to fire and poison, though it can also turn magic aside.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Blisterwort				|A tall cave mushroom with a rough, blistered cap. Odd as it seems, it's one of the few ingredients a smith has any use for: one of its effects steadies the hand at the forge.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BlueButterflyWing		|The wing of a blue butterfly, caught over Skyrim's meadows. Enchanters seek them out, since a potion of them makes an enchantment take more strongly.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BlueDartwing			|A blue dragonfly that skims over streams and ponds. Thieves have a quiet fondness for it: one of its effects makes light fingers lighter still.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BlueMountainFlower		|One of the commonest flowers in Skyrim, growing along the roads and hillsides of almost every hold. Paired with wheat it brews into a fine healing potion, and it's often the first an apprentice learns.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BoneMeal				|Ground from the bones of the dead, most often taken from the skeletons that walk in old tombs. Necromancers find it useful, for reasons best left unasked.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_BriarHeart				|The heart a hagraven's magic plants in the chest of a Forsworn Briarheart, keeping the warrior alive and fighting. Take it from one and the Briarheart falls.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_ButterflyWing			|The orange and black wing of a monarch butterfly, found fluttering over the flowers of Skyrim's milder holds. A merchant's favourite, since one of its effects makes for better prices.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_CanisRoot				|A root dug from Skyrim's wilds. Archers prize it, and so does anyone who wants a target to stay still.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_CharredSkeeverHide		|What's left of a skeever roasted on a spit, as found over the campfires of bandits and others who can't afford better. Burnt as it is, it's surprisingly good at curing what ails you.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_ChaurusEggs				|Laid by the chaurus, the great insects the Falmer keep in the caves beneath Skyrim. The eggs are taken from their nests, at some risk to the one taking them.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_ChickensEgg				|An ordinary hen's egg from the nests around Skyrim's farms. A humble thing, but with the right partner it lets you breathe underwater.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_CreepCluster			|A rock-hugging plant of the volcanic tundra around Eastmarch's hot springs. Its tangled growth breaks away easily in the hand.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_CrimsonNirnroot			|A red nirnroot that grows only in Blackreach, the vast cavern beneath Skyrim. Like its common cousin it chimes faintly, and the alchemist Sinderion died down there studying it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_CyrodilicSpadetail		|A fish named for Cyrodiil and for the flat, spade-like tail it swims with. In Skyrim it's found in the rivers and lakes.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_DaedraHeart				|The heart of a dremora, still faintly warm with the power of Oblivion. Rare and costly: the few merchants who have one ask a high price for it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Deathbell				|A drooping flower of the marshes of Hjaalmarch, its name honestly earned. Ingun Black-Briar in Riften wants some for her studies.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_DragonsTongue			|A bright orange flower from the volcanic tundra of Eastmarch. A potion made from it helps you stand against fire, a dragon's breath included.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_DwarvenOil				|Oil drained from the broken automatons that still guard the Dwemer ruins. After all these centuries it still runs.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Ectoplasm				|The glowing residue a ghost leaves behind when it's laid to rest. Destruction mages are fond of it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_ElvesEar				|A plant with long, pointed leaves that give it its name. Archers make good use of it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_EyeOfSabreCat			|Taken from a sabre cat, one of the most dangerous hunters in Skyrim. Despite where it comes from, it restores both stamina and health.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_FalmerEar				|Taken from the Falmer, the blind elves of Skyrim's deepest caves. A grim trophy, but a useful one for anyone who picks locks.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_FireSalts				|The fiery remains of a flame atronach, still warm with the fire that made it. Mages pay well for them.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_FlyAmanita				|A red mushroom spotted with white, a familiar sight in Skyrim's caves. Its effects range from warding off fire to driving people into a frenzy.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_FrostMirriam			|A hardy herb of the snowy north, growing where little else will. It helps the drinker go unnoticed.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_FrostSalts				|The icy remains of a frost atronach, and among the most valuable ingredients there are. Conjurers like them for the way they lengthen a summons.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Garlic					|A kitchen staple, hung in strings in many Skyrim homes. Old wisdom says it keeps vampires away; alchemists know it better for helping wounds heal.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_GiantLichen				|A grey-green lichen that clings to the rocks in the marshes of Hjaalmarch. Much of what it does is harmful, but it restores magicka too.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_GiantsToe				|The toe of a giant, taken at great risk from one of the herders who drive their mammoths across the plains. Fittingly, it lets you carry more.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_GlowDust				|The shimmering dust left when a wisp or wispmother is destroyed. It still gives off a faint light of its own.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_GlowingMushroom			|A luminous fungus that lights the caves and Dwemer ruins beneath Skyrim, nowhere more than Blackreach.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_GrassPod				|The seed pod of the spiky grass that grows in northern Skyrim. Light and common, it's useful to mages who work with Alteration.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HagravenClaw			|A claw from a hagraven, one of the crones who trade their humanity for power and keep company with the Forsworn. Enchanters value it.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HagravenFeathers		|Feathers from a hagraven. They carry something of the creature's foul magic, which conjurers find useful.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HangingMoss				|A grey moss that hangs in curtains from the trees of Skyrim's damp forests and marshes.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HawkBeak				|Taken from the hawks that circle over Skyrim's plains and mountains. It takes a good bow to bring one down.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HawkFeathers			|Feathers from a hawk, light and strong. Alchemists use them for potions of light armour and a light step.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Histcarp				|A fish whose name recalls the Hist of Black Marsh, though it's quite at home in Skyrim's waters. Useful for breathing underwater.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Honeycomb				|A piece of comb from a beehive, dripping with honey. Good to eat, and better still for anyone who wants a sturdier guard.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HumanFlesh				|Flesh taken from the dead by those who feed on it, Namira's cannibals among them. Best not to ask where any particular piece came from.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_HumanHeart				|A human heart, cut out for dark rites. Only a handful are to be found in Skyrim, in the lairs of those who use them.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_IceWraithTeeth			|The teeth of an ice wraith, the serpent-like spirits of Skyrim's snowfields and frozen peaks. One of the few ingredients that can make you invisible.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_ImpStool				|A cave mushroom with tall, narrow caps. Most of what it does is harmful, though it can heal as well.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_JarrinRoot				|The only one in Skyrim, handed over by Astrid for the Dark Brotherhood's plot against the Emperor. Every one of its effects is harmful.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_JazbayGrapes			|A small purple grape that grows wild in Eastmarch, around Windhelm. Mages favour it for their magicka.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_JuniperBerries			|Blue-black berries from the juniper bushes on the hillsides of the Reach. Archers and the wounded both have uses for them.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_LargeAntlers			|A large set of antlers taken from an elk. Hunters and alchemists both keep them.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Lavender				|A purple flower that grows wild on the plains around Whiterun. Its scent calms, and its effects help guard against magic.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_LunaMothWing			|The pale green wing of a luna moth, a night-flying moth of Skyrim's woods. One of the few ingredients that can make you invisible.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_MoonSugar				|The sweet crystals the Khajiit bring from Elsweyr, and the stuff skooma is made from. It can't be found in the wild; Khajiit traders are the only source.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_MoraTapinella			|A shelf fungus that grows on fallen logs and stumps in Skyrim's forests. Illusionists use it to strengthen their spells.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_MudcrabChitin			|A piece of a mudcrab's shell. Mudcrabs are everywhere along Skyrim's shores, and anyone who's walked by a river has met one.

UI_Ingredients_Lore_Nightshade				|A dark-leaved plant with drooping purple flowers, at home in shaded woods. Every herbalist's first lesson is to leave it alone, and every poisoner's is the opposite. Ingun Black-Briar in Riften wants some for her studies.
UI_Ingredients_Lore_Nirnroot				|A plant that grows by water and gives off a faint chime, so it's often heard before it's seen. It's named after Nirn itself, and Ingun Black-Briar in Riften wants some for her studies.

UI_Ingredients_Effect_CureDisease				|Clears every disease you've caught, from the rattles to ataxia. Cheaper than a shrine, and it doesn't mind which god you pray to.

UI_Ingredients_Effect_FortifyStamina			|Raises your stamina for a while.

UI_Ingredients_Effect_Frenzy					|Drives anyone up to a certain level to attack whatever's near them, friend or foe, for a while.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- UI: Guided tour (UI_Tour_*)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------
UI_Tour_OfferTitle				|New here?
UI_Tour_OfferText				|Completionist's window has a new look. A tour shows you where everything is: the different kinds of page, the panels, the Cell Scanner and the settings. You can take it again any time from Settings.
UI_Tour_Take					|Take the tour
UI_Tour_NotNow					|Not now
UI_Tour_Next					|Next
UI_Tour_Back					|Back
UI_Tour_Skip					|End tour
UI_Tour_Finish					|Finish
UI_Tour_Step{}{}				|{} of {}
UI_Tour_WelcomeTitle			|Welcome
UI_Tour_WelcomeText				|This tour takes you round the window one part at a time. It takes a few minutes, and you can end it whenever you like.
UI_Tour_SidebarTitle			|Pages
UI_Tour_SidebarText				|Everything Completionist tracks is listed here: quests, collections, locations and the patches you have installed. Pick a page to open it, or step through them with the shoulder buttons on a controller. Double-click the grip beside the list to fold it away and give the page more room.
UI_Tour_OverviewTitle			|Overview
UI_Tour_OverviewText			|With no page open you see the overview: how far you've got in each group, and the things you found most recently.
UI_Tour_HeaderTitle				|Find and Cell Scanner
UI_Tour_HeaderText				|Find searches every page at once, so you can look anything up by name. Cell Scanner shows what's still to find around you. We'll look at it in a moment.
UI_Tour_EntriesTitle			|The list
UI_Tour_EntriesText				|Each page lists what there is to find, and marks what you've found. Point at a row to see its details below. Depending on the page, the button at the end of a row ticks it off by hand, pins it, or tracks its location on your map.
UI_Tour_PageToolsTitle			|Filter and sort
UI_Tour_PageToolsText			|Type here to filter the list by name, hide what you've already found, or change the order. The bar shows how far you've got on this page. Pages with tabs switch between them with the triggers on a controller.
UI_Tour_DescriptionTitle		|Details
UI_Tour_DescriptionText			|Details of the row you point at: where to find it and anything else worth knowing. Drag the grip on its top edge to make it taller or shorter, or double-click the grip to fold it.
UI_Tour_PinsTitle				|Pins and markers
UI_Tour_PinsText				|Two ways to go after something. Pin an item and the game marks it for you whenever you're in the same cell as it, and a bar at the top of the window lists your pins. Track location puts a quest marker on a place or person straight away. There are only so many tracking slots, so clear one when you're done with it.
UI_Tour_QuestsTitle				|Quest pages
UI_Tour_QuestsText				|Quest pages work like your journal: what's still open on one side and what you've completed on the other. Select a quest to read about it below. Some pages depend on a choice you make, such as your side in the civil war or the Dawnguard: those fill in once it's made.
UI_Tour_TrainersTitle			|Trainers
UI_Tour_TrainersText			|Every trainer, split into Combat, Magic and Stealth tabs. Each one shows their tier, how many levels they can still teach you, and where they are if they've wandered from home. It also shows how far you've got through that skill's perks.
UI_Tour_DragonsTitle			|Dragons
UI_Tour_DragonsText				|The named dragons and their lore, with what's become of each one, on the first tab. The second tab counts every dragon you've killed. Dragons added by other mods get their own Installed Content section.
UI_Tour_IngredientsTitle		|Ingredients
UI_Tour_IngredientsText			|Ingredients sorted into tabs, the diamonds beside each one showing how many of its effects you've discovered. Its details suggest what to brew it with to learn an unknown effect, using what you carry. The Effects tab goes by effect, and the Mixing Station tab has the options for naming undiscovered effects and showing pictures.
UI_Tour_KillsTitle				|Kill Counts
UI_Tour_KillsText				|What you've killed, creature by creature: your kills, your assists, and the type you've slain most. Sort it by kills or assists, and reset a count if you want to start one again.
UI_Tour_AchievementsTitle		|Achievements
UI_Tour_AchievementsText		|The game's achievements in one place, with this save's progress towards each one, a tip on how to get it, how rare it is on Steam, and a warning on any you can lock yourself out of. General Settings chooses what's shown, or hides the page.
UI_Tour_MuseumTitle				|Museum Displays
UI_Tour_MuseumText				|With Legacy of the Dragonborn, this shows what's on show in the museum right now, room by room, including sections added by patches. It also says whether you're carrying what a display needs.
UI_Tour_CellListTitle			|Cell Scanner
UI_Tour_CellListText			|The Cell Scanner lists everything still to find in the area you're in, with how far away it is. Pick an item to put a quest marker on it, so you can walk straight to it.
UI_Tour_CellKey{}				|Open it straight from the game with {}.
UI_Tour_CellNoKey				|You can give it its own key in Settings, to open it straight from the game.
UI_Tour_CellOptionsTitle		|Scanner options
UI_Tour_CellOptionsText			|Set how the scanner searches, what it leaves out, and how pinned items are shown. Click the heading to fold the options away.
UI_Tour_CellBarTitle			|Scanner bar
UI_Tour_CellBarText				|Show height tells you whether an item is above or below you. Rescan looks again, and in an interior you can exclude the cell once you're done with it. Keep on screen puts the scanner on screen while you play: that's next.
UI_Tour_OnScreenTitle			|Always on screen
UI_Tour_OnScreenText			|While you play, Keep on screen shows the Cell Scanner on screen: the closest things still to find, how far away they are and which way to go. Completionist's own notifications show here too, when you find something. Settings > Window turns the panel on or off, and the Place UI elements button on Settings > HUD & Notifications moves it and the notifications anywhere you like, or joins the two.
UI_Tour_SettingsTitle			|Settings
UI_Tour_SettingsText			|The cog at the top opens Settings. This first tab is the window itself: its theme, size, keys and controller buttons. Point at any setting and the panel at the bottom explains what it does.
UI_Tour_SettingsGeneralTitle	|General Settings
UI_Tour_SettingsGeneralText		|What counts as finished. Set how many times each kind of repeatable quest must be done, and choose your side where a story branches, so the right quests are listed. What the Achievements page shows is here too.
UI_Tour_SettingsHudTitle		|HUD & Notifications
UI_Tour_SettingsHudText			|What Completionist tells you while you play. Choose which notifications show and where, the tags on your crosshair, and how item names appear in menus. Further down are the icons in your inventory, containers and shops, each with its own colours, and the COMPLETIONIST sort for those lists.
UI_Tour_SettingsMuseumTitle		|Museum Mode
UI_Tour_SettingsMuseumText		|Tags and icons for museum items, even ones Completionist doesn't track. Museum Items Only quiets everything except museum items and specials like shrines and fish. Pages and tracking carry on underneath, so turning it off loses nothing.
UI_Tour_SettingsLogTitle		|Completion Log
UI_Tour_SettingsLogText			|A record of what you've found and finished, by the date you did it. Pick a date to read that day back.
UI_Tour_PadTitle				|With a controller
UI_Tour_PadText					|Everything works with a controller too, and the buttons do the same job on every screen: the shoulder buttons step through pages and the triggers through tabs. This bar shows what each button does right now, and changes as you move around the window.
UI_Tour_OpenKey{}				|Open this window with {}.
UI_Tour_DoneTitle				|That's the tour
UI_Tour_DoneText				|You can take it again any time with this button.
UI_SettingsSection_Help			|Help
UI_Setting_Tour					|Guided tour
UI_Setting_TourStart			|Take the tour
UI_SettingHint_Tour				|Shows you round the window one part at a time: the pages, the panels, the Cell Scanner and the settings.
